sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the year 1623, Christian IV, king of Denmark and Norway,
sentences.zh: 1623年，丹麦和挪威国王克里斯蒂安四世，

sentences.en: built a long series of moats and ramparts just across from central Copenhagen,
sentences.zh: 在哥本哈根市中心对面修建了一系列护城河和壁垒，

sentences.en: on the eastern edge of the city's harbor.
sentences.zh: 位于城市港口的东缘。

sentences.en: For much of the 17th century, the fortification protected the city from Swedish invasion.
sentences.zh: 在17世纪的大部分时间里，这些防御工事保护着这座城市免受瑞典的入侵。

sentences.en: In the early 19th century, the Danish government added artillery barracks.
sentences.zh: 19世纪初，丹麦政府增建了炮兵营房。

sentences.en: And in the 20th century, they filled in the surrounding swamps
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪，他们填平了周围的沼泽，

sentences.en: to make room for a modern military base, even as the rest of Copenhagen grew around it.
sentences.zh: 为现代军事基地腾出空间，尽管哥本哈根的其他部分已经在它周围发展起来。

sentences.en: That is, until 1971, when the sprawling fortress in the center of the city
sentences.zh: 直到1971年，市中心那片庞大的堡垒，

sentences.en: transformed into something else entirely.
sentences.zh: 彻底变成了另一种东西。

sentences.en: And it started off with the kids who had, of course, been wondering what goes on in there.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于那些一直好奇里面到底在发生什么的孩子们。

sentences.en: They saw the soldiers coming in and out, they heard the military music,
sentences.zh: 他们看到士兵进进出出，听到军乐声，

sentences.en: but they were now never allowed to go in there.
sentences.zh: 但他们却从未被允许进入其中。

sentences.en: John Bank Carlson was in his early 20s when he moved to Copenhagen
sentences.zh: 约翰·班克·卡尔森20出头时从丹麦乡村保守的家中搬到了哥本哈根，

sentences.en: from his conservative home in the Danish countryside.
sentences.zh: 他搬到了哥本哈根。

sentences.en: And he says the symbolism of a military base in the heart of the country's capital
sentences.zh: 他说，在国家首都中心设立军事基地的象征意义，

sentences.en: was not lost on him and his friends.
sentences.zh: 他和他的朋友们都心知肚明。

sentences.en: That's reporter Scott Gurian.
sentences.zh: 那是记者斯科特·古里安。

sentences.en: The base's walls represented authority, repression,
sentences.zh: 基地的围墙代表着权威、压迫，

sentences.en: pretty much everything Denmark's younger generation had come to Copenhagen to escape.
sentences.zh: 几乎是丹麦年轻一代来到哥本哈根想要逃离的一切。

sentences.en: But in 1971, the Danish defense ministry decided they no longer needed the base,
sentences.zh: 但在1971年，丹麦国防部决定不再需要这个基地，

sentences.en: and they closed it for good.
sentences.zh: 于是彻底关闭了它。

sentences.en: So suddenly, one morning, we see all the soldiers marching out of there,
sentences.zh: 所以突然有一天早上，我们看到所有的士兵从里面撤出，

sentences.en: you know, see all the vehicles leave, the military vehicles leave,
sentences.zh: 你知道，看到所有的车辆离开，军用车辆离开，

sentences.en: and they don't close the door.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有关门。

sentences.en: John speaking figuratively, technically, the doors were locked.
sentences.zh: 约翰说的是比喻，从技术上讲，门是锁着的。

sentences.en: But people living nearby realized they could break in, and no one would stop them.
sentences.zh: 但住在附近的人意识到他们可以闯进去，而且没人会阻止他们。

sentences.en: Somehow, the army, the big, big father figure,
sentences.zh: 不知何故，军队，那个庞大的、伟大的父亲形象，

sentences.en: had kind of died in our middle, in the middle of the city, right?
sentences.zh: 在我们中间，在城市中心死去了，对吧？

sentences.en: And we could just crawl over the walls.
sentences.zh: 我们可以直接翻过围墙。

sentences.en: And like two weeks before, we would have been shot if we did the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而在两周前，如果我们做同样的事，我们会被枪毙的。

sentences.en: Like any young person who comes across an abandoned, boarded-up property,
sentences.zh: 就像任何偶然发现废弃、封板房产的年轻人一样，

sentences.en: John was curious to explore.
sentences.zh: 约翰很好奇，想要一探究竟。

sentences.en: The first evening, he climbed over the barbed wire walls.
sentences.zh: 第一个晚上，他翻过了带刺铁丝网的围墙。

sentences.en: The interior of the base was dark.
sentences.zh: 基地内部一片漆黑。

sentences.en: He couldn't see much other than the broken glass from kids who had already vandalized the former barracks.
sentences.zh: 除了那些已经破坏了前营房的孩子们留下的碎玻璃，他看不清什么。

sentences.en: But as the sun rose, it became clear to John just what he and the other trespassers had on their hands.
sentences.zh: 但随着太阳升起，约翰清楚地意识到他和那些闯入者手里拥有的是什么。

sentences.en: This was not some cramped, depressing concrete jungle.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是什么狭窄、压抑的混凝土丛林。

sentences.en: Instead, the world within the fortress's walls was almost rural.
sentences.zh: 相反，堡垒围墙内的世界几乎是田园诗般的。

sentences.en: At 85 acres, the base contained vast green spaces, hills, patches of foreSt.
sentences.zh: 基地占地85英亩，拥有广阔的绿地、山丘和成片的森林。

sentences.en: There was even a lake with the hulking shapes of empty stables and ammunition depots scattered in charming arrangements around the landscape.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一个湖泊，湖边散落着空荡荡的马厩和弹药库，呈现出迷人的布局。

sentences.en: And the trespassers wasted no time making themselves at home.
sentences.zh: 闯入者们毫不耽搁，立刻安顿了下来。

sentences.en: And whatever we wanted to do, we were free to do it.
sentences.zh: 无论我们想做什么，我们都可以自由去做。

sentences.en: We could snap up whatever house.
sentences.zh: 我们可以抢占任何房子。

sentences.en: If we wanted 2,000 square meters to live on, we could do that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想住2000平方米的地方，我们就可以做到。

sentences.en: And where I finally ended up was a beautiful, beautiful old farm, you know,
sentences.zh: 我最终落脚的地方是一个美丽、美丽的老农场，你知道，

sentences.en: wonderful reflection of beautiful trees, you know, around the lake.
sentences.zh: 湖边美丽的树木倒影，真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And the only thing that reminded you of the city was you could hear the police sirens.
sentences.zh: 唯一让你想起城市的就是你能听到警笛声。

sentences.en: But visually, it was like paradise somehow.
sentences.zh: 但从视觉上看，它不知何故就像天堂一样。

sentences.en: John and the other trespassers ended up squatting in various buildings throughout the base.
sentences.zh: 约翰和其他闯入者最终在基地各处的建筑物里非法居住。

sentences.en: And as word spread, the abandoned compound quickly became a haven for the unwanted, the abused, and the dispossessed.
sentences.zh: 随着消息传开，这个废弃的院落迅速成为被遗弃者、受虐待者和无家可归者的避风港。

sentences.en: A lot of the kids that came there were from very poor backgrounds, you know,
sentences.zh: 很多来到那里的孩子都来自非常贫困的背景，你知道，

sentences.en: runaways from being mistreated sexually or people who came out of jail and had nowhere to go.
sentences.zh: 遭受性虐待的逃家者，或者刚出狱无处可去的人。

sentences.en: People who otherwise would be put into institutions.
sentences.zh: 那些本会被送进收容机构的人。

sentences.en: So suddenly this corpse of a military army base was beginning to resurrect,
sentences.zh: 所以突然间，这具军事基地的尸体开始复活，

sentences.en: but resurrect as something which was in total disaccord with what it originally was meant to be.
sentences.zh: 但复活后的样子与它最初的用途完全不符。

sentences.en: And it was during their first few weeks that the ragtag group of squatters decided to get organized.
sentences.zh: 就在最初的几周里，这群乌合之众的非法居住者决定组织起来。

sentences.en: They declared the base a, quote, politically autonomous anarchist zone, or in plainer English, a commune.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布该基地为“政治自治无政府主义区”，用更通俗的话说，就是一个公社。

sentences.en: Only this commune would become far larger and more consequential than anyone outside could have imagined.
sentences.zh: 只是这个公社变得比外界任何人想象的都要大得多，影响也深远得多。

sentences.en: Like many other communes, the founders wanted the new world they made within the walls,
sentences.zh: 像许多其他公社一样，创始人们希望他们在围墙内创造的新世界，

sentences.en: to be as free as possible from all the old world's rules and customs and hierarchies.
sentences.zh: 尽可能地摆脱旧世界所有的规则、习俗和等级制度。

sentences.en: We suddenly had a chance to kind of say, okay, we don't know what happens.
sentences.zh: 我们突然有机会说，好吧，我们不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: We don't know anything.
sentences.zh: 我们什么都不知道。

sentences.en: We have to create our own society.
sentences.zh: 我们必须创造我们自己的社会。

sentences.en: And it was a little like a beautiful blank piece of paper,
sentences.zh: 这就像一张美丽的白纸，

sentences.en: and you could start writing a new story, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以开始书写一个新的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: They drew up a mission statement, according to which the goal of the commune was, quote,
sentences.zh: 他们起草了一份使命宣言，根据该宣言，公社的目标是，引用如下：

sentences.en: to create a self-governing society whereby each and every individual holds themselves responsible
sentences.zh: 创建一个自治社会，每个个体都对自己负责，

sentences.en: for the well-being of the entire community.
sentences.zh: 为整个社区的福祉负责。

sentences.en: They also settled on a name, taking a cue from the surrounding Christians Harbor neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们还确定了一个名字，从周围的克里斯蒂安港社区中汲取了灵感。

sentences.en: They called their community Christiania.
sentences.zh: 他们把自己的社区称为“克里斯蒂安尼亚”。

sentences.en: But unlike a lot of other idealistic communities of the 60s and 70s,
sentences.zh: 但与60和70年代许多其他理想主义社区不同，

sentences.en: Christiania is still around, and in many ways, it has achieved the dreams of its founders.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚依然存在，并且在许多方面实现了其创始人的梦想。

sentences.en: Today, it's one of the longest-lasting and most celebrated communes in the world,
sentences.zh: 今天，它是世界上存在时间最长、最著名的公社之一，

sentences.en: and a magnet for people searching for alternative ways of living,
sentences.zh: 也是寻找替代生活方式的人们的磁石，

sentences.en: existing both side-by-side and within a major European city.
sentences.zh: 它既与欧洲大城市并存，又身处其中。

sentences.en: But in recent years, Christiania's residents have faced an increasing number of threats
sentences.zh: 但近年来，克里斯蒂安尼亚的居民面临着越来越多的威胁，

sentences.en: that have raised tough questions about the limits of autonomy,
sentences.zh: 这些威胁提出了关于自治极限的棘手问题，

sentences.en: about how much individual freedom might be too much,
sentences.zh: 关于个人自由究竟多少才算过头，

sentences.en: and whether to hold onto tradition or change with a changing world.
sentences.zh: 以及是坚守传统还是随世界变化而改变。

sentences.en: And now, people both inside and outside Christiania's walls
sentences.zh: 现在，克里斯蒂安尼亚围墙内外的人们，

sentences.en: are wondering how much longer this utopian experiment can ultimately laSt.
sentences.zh: 都在想这个乌托邦实验最终还能持续多久。

sentences.en: Christiania, of course, people moved in to find a place to live,
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚，当然，人们搬进来是为了找个住处，

sentences.en: but people very definitely moved into Christiania
sentences.zh: 但人们非常明确地搬进克里斯蒂安尼亚，

sentences.en: to be part of making a city that was based on other ideas than the rest of society.
sentences.zh: 是为了参与建设一个基于与社会其他部分不同理念的城市。

sentences.en: This is Ole Luke Andersen, another early Christiania resident.
sentences.zh: 这是奥勒·卢克·安徒生，另一位早期的克里斯蒂安尼亚居民。

sentences.en: Ole arrived in the late 1970s,
sentences.zh: 奥勒在70年代末抵达，

sentences.en: and he described to me what the scene was like
sentences.zh: 他向我描述了当时的情景，

sentences.en: after John and the other squatters settled in.
sentences.zh: 在约翰和其他非法居住者定居之后。

sentences.en: Christiania was tough to move into.
sentences.zh: 搬进克里斯蒂安尼亚很艰难。

sentences.en: Two-thirds of Christiania had no infrastructure at all.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚三分之二的地方根本没有基础设施。

sentences.en: In other words, they might have had all those big old buildings
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们可能拥有所有那些又大又旧的建筑，

sentences.en: and the basic shelter they needed, but very little else.
sentences.zh: 以及他们所需的基本住所，但几乎没有其他东西。

sentences.en: You had to make heating systems yourself.
sentences.zh: 你必须自己制造供暖系统。

sentences.en: You had to work with the stewards and electricity and water supply.
sentences.zh: 你必须处理水电供应问题。

sentences.en: So it was like moving into the Wild West in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像在70年代搬进了狂野西部。

sentences.en: And so the commune's residents got to work.
sentences.zh: 于是公社的居民们开始行动起来。

sentences.en: They adapted the existing structures,
sentences.zh: 他们改造了现有的结构，

sentences.en: building fantastical homes out of recycled objects
sentences.zh: 用回收物品建造了奇幻的房屋，

sentences.en: and filling them with amazing art.
sentences.zh: 并用令人惊叹的艺术品装饰它们。

sentences.en: They turned a former stable into a church
sentences.zh: 他们把一个旧马厩变成了教堂，

sentences.en: and transformed a military horse-riding arena into a concert hall.
sentences.zh: 把一个军用骑马场改造成了音乐厅。

sentences.en: This is Christiania, a community of a thousand hippies and assorted dogs.
sentences.zh: 这就是克里斯蒂安尼亚，一个由一千名嬉皮士和各种狗组成的社区。

sentences.en: There are small businesses, a factory that makes customized bicycles,
sentences.zh: 这里有小企业，一家制造定制自行车的工厂，

sentences.en: a women's blacksmith shop,
sentences.zh: 一家女性铁匠铺，

sentences.en: completely surrounded by Copenhagen's old city.
sentences.zh: 完全被哥本哈根的老城区所包围。

sentences.en: Christiania wasn't totally cut off from the outside world.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚并没有完全与外界隔绝。

sentences.en: Its residents would engage in commerce and come and go into the rest of the city.
sentences.zh: 居民们会进行商业活动，并往返于城市的其他地方。

sentences.en: But inside the walls, the community collected its own trash and recycling,
sentences.zh: 但在围墙内，社区收集自己的垃圾和回收物，

sentences.en: operated its own kindergarten,
sentences.zh: 经营自己的幼儿园，

sentences.en: and even had its own newspaper and marching band.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有自己的报纸和军乐队。

sentences.en: Aside from a small shared maintenance fee,
sentences.zh: 除了少量的共享维护费外，

sentences.en: residents paid no rent.
sentences.zh: 居民无需支付租金。

sentences.en: No one owned their home.
sentences.zh: 没有人拥有自己的房子。

sentences.en: And when they moved out, there was nothing to sell.
sentences.zh: 当他们搬走时，也没有什么可卖的。

sentences.en: There were no building or zoning codes.
sentences.zh: 没有建筑或分区法规。

sentences.en: There were also no laws.
sentences.zh: 也没有法律。

sentences.en: The only rules were no private ownership of land or housing,
sentences.zh: 唯一的规则是土地或住房不得私有，

sentences.en: no weapons or violence,
sentences.zh: 禁止武器或暴力，

sentences.en: and no vehicles.
sentences.zh: 禁止车辆。

sentences.en: Otherwise, people in Christiania were pretty much free to do whatever they wanted.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，克里斯蒂安尼亚的人们几乎可以自由地做任何他们想做的事。

sentences.en: Play rock music in the streets,
sentences.zh: 在街上演奏摇滚乐，

sentences.en: do drugs,
sentences.zh: 吸毒，

sentences.en: sell drugs,
sentences.zh: 贩毒，

sentences.en: wear their hair long or shave it off,
sentences.zh: 留长发或剃光头，

sentences.en: love members of the same sex or a different race.
sentences.zh: 爱上同性或不同种族的人。

sentences.en: All the things, in other words,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，所有那些，

sentences.en: that were still dangerous or impossible in the world outside its gates.
sentences.zh: 在围墙外世界依然危险或不可能做到的事情。

sentences.en: John told me about a woman who spent her days roller skating around naked,
sentences.zh: 约翰告诉我一个女人整天赤身裸体地滑旱冰，

sentences.en: and even a guy who kept a pet bear that he fed beer.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一个家伙养了一只喂啤酒的宠物熊。

sentences.en: It always looked slightly drunk.
sentences.zh: 它看起来总是有点醉醺醺的。

sentences.en: It was big.
sentences.zh: 它很大。

sentences.en: It was rather big.
sentences.zh: 它相当大。

sentences.en: How did he end up with a bear?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么弄到一只熊的？

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道那个。

sentences.en: I don't know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道那个。

sentences.en: But amid the craziness,
sentences.zh: 但在疯狂之中，

sentences.en: there were also moments of incredible beauty.
sentences.zh: 也有令人难以置信的美丽时刻。

sentences.en: Like the story John told me from his first winter at the base
sentences.zh: 就像约翰告诉我的他在基地度过的第一个冬天的故事，

sentences.en: about a former ammunition depot someone had turned into a house.
sentences.zh: 关于一个被某人改造成房子的前弹药库。

sentences.en: And suddenly one day when I passed it,
sentences.zh: 突然有一天我经过那里时，

sentences.en: you heard the most beautiful piano kind of playing Chopin.
sentences.zh: 你听到了最美妙的钢琴声，好像在演奏肖邦。

sentences.en: And then you went into this building,
sentences.zh: 然后你走进这座建筑，

sentences.en: and in this huge room there was this little tent.
sentences.zh: 在这个巨大的房间里有一个小帐篷。

sentences.en: And inside the tent you can see kind of the silhouette of a grand piano.
sentences.zh: 在帐篷里，你可以看到一架三角钢琴的轮廓。

sentences.en: And I looked in, and here was this kind of very refined artistic guy
sentences.zh: 我往里看，这里有一个非常精致的艺术家，

sentences.en: sitting and playing beautifully on the piano.
sentences.zh: 坐着，优美地弹奏着钢琴。

sentences.en: You never forget that stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 你永远不会忘记那些东西，对吧？

sentences.en: The individual freedom on offer in Christiania
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚所提供的个人自由

sentences.en: attracted people from around the world.
sentences.zh: 吸引了来自世界各地的人们。

sentences.en: But there were other advantages too,
sentences.zh: 但这里还有其他优势，

sentences.en: like how it had its own way of settling disputes
sentences.zh: 比如它有自己解决纠纷的方式，

sentences.en: and making collective decisions.
sentences.zh: 以及做出集体决策的方法。

sentences.en: Well, what appealed about it to me would be like
sentences.zh: 嗯，它吸引我的地方在于，

sentences.en: every opinion gets heard and respected a lot.
sentences.zh: 每个人的意见都能得到倾听和高度尊重。

sentences.en: Mario Sarasco moved to Christiania from Boston in the early 1980s,
sentences.zh: 马里奥·萨拉斯科在20世纪80年代初从波士顿搬到了克里斯蒂安尼亚，

sentences.en: a little after John and Ole.
sentences.zh: 比约翰和奥勒晚了一点。

sentences.en: And he says one of the big things he appreciated about the community
sentences.zh: 他说他非常欣赏这个社区的一大特色，

sentences.en: that made Christiania different in the first place.

sentences.zh: 我们无法与这些人沟通。

sentences.zh: 你参与了？

sentences.en: Actually, to block it, if we could.
sentences.zh: 那真是一种解脱。

sentences.zh: 让人无法进入。

sentences.zh: 然后我们就那样离开了。

sentences.en: and concrete blocks on either side of the street, making it impossible for people to enter.
sentences.zh: 毒贩们早上 8 点就回来了。

sentences.en: And then sort of we left it.
sentences.zh: 他们很生气。

sentences.zh: 而且非常生气。

sentences.en: And they were angry.

sentences.en: And they were very angry.
sentences.zh: 所以到了 12 点，一切又恢复原样了。

sentences.en: And like 10 o'clock, they actually managed to find a way to move the containers.
sentences.zh: 你当时预料到封锁会持续更久吗？

sentences.en: So at 12 o'clock, everything was open again.
sentences.zh: 我确实预料到它会持续久一点，是的。

sentences.en: Were you expecting that the blockade would last longer?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I expected it to last a little longer, yes.
sentences.zh: 但我没指望它真的能一直持续下去，没有。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们没能移开集装箱并重新开放普舍街，

sentences.zh: 你们会遇到大麻烦的。

sentences.en: Because if they had not managed to move the containers and reopen Pusher Street,
sentences.zh: 他们会寻求报复的。

sentences.en: you would have had a lot of trouble.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，克里斯蒂安尼亚手无寸铁的居民对帮派唯一能采取的行动，

sentences.en: They would have sought revenge.
sentences.zh: 纯粹是象征性的。

sentences.zh: 这项行动不仅没有在共识会议上得到广大社区的同意，

sentences.en: was purely symbolic.
sentences.zh: 而且居民们也知道，仅仅说他们想关闭普舍街，

sentences.en: Not only had the action not been agreed on by the larger community in a consensus meeting,
sentences.zh: 并不会带来任何改变。

sentences.zh: 面对禁令，毒贩们只会拒绝离开。

sentences.en: wouldn't make a difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么一些居民想要推翻另一项长期存在的传统。

sentences.en: Faced with a ban, the dealers would just refuse to leave.
sentences.zh: 如果社区最终同意关闭普舍街，

sentences.en: Which is why some of the residents wanted to reverse another long-standing tradition.
sentences.zh: 他们还想发表一份公开声明，称他们无力独自完成这件事。

sentences.en: If the community finally agreed to close Pusher Street,
sentences.zh: 本质上，就是邀请警察进来替他们强制执行关闭。

sentences.en: they also wanted to issue a public statement saying that they were powerless to do it on their own.
sentences.zh: 没有人没意识到这其中的讽刺意味。

sentences.en: Essentially, inviting the police to come in and enforce the closure for them.
sentences.zh: 公社居民一生都在努力尝试在没有国家和国家暴力作为组织力量的情况下生活。

sentences.en: The irony of which was not lost on anyone.
sentences.zh: 但现在，如果他们想最终把帮派赶走，

sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚的无政府主义者就不得不向国家寻求帮助。

sentences.en: and state violence as an organizing force.
sentences.zh: 所以不知何故，警察赢了。

sentences.en: But now, if they wanted to finally kick the gangs out,
sentences.zh: 你面对所有的帮派，但警察无疑是最强大的帮派。

sentences.zh: 社区最近是否与警方和市政府进行了对话，

sentences.zh: 让你觉得现在比过去更信任他们了？

sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: We have talks, but, you know, personally, I don't trust them.
sentences.zh: 是的，那真是一种奇怪的感觉。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 在最近一次暴力事件激增之后，在路障之夜后不久，

sentences.en: you know, we're like inviting the police to help us out?
sentences.zh: 这是他们经常用于重要集会的大型音乐会场地。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was really a strange feeling.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有半个小时非常特别的时间，

sentences.zh: 人们只是走到麦克风前，没有发表任何演讲。

sentences.zh: 他们只是说，比如，我想关闭普舍街。

sentences.en: this large concert venue they often use for important gatherings.
sentences.zh: 我想关闭普舍街。

sentences.zh: 这对于那些不想这样做的少数派来说，竟然如此具有说服力。

sentences.zh: 这些帮派一直都在，带着刀子，你知道的，

sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们就有了枪。

sentences.zh: 毕竟，他们只是一群热爱和平的嬉皮士。

sentences.zh: 会议就这样结束了。

sentences.zh: 听奥勒（Ole）说，共识机制发挥了它应有的作用。

sentences.zh: 它达成了共识。

sentences.zh: 但一些居民却有不同的看法。

sentences.zh: 他们说，共识机制只是克里斯蒂安尼亚（Christiania）又一个开始瓦解的传统。

sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚内部对此完全没有达成一致。

sentences.zh: 决定做出后不久，我在一场关于大麻合法化的活动外遇到了马里奥·萨拉斯科（Mario Sarasco），

sentences.zh: 那是克里斯蒂安尼亚吸引我的自由的一部分。

sentences.zh: 我要把它放在柏林墙的鹅卵石旁边。

sentences.en: So, Marios, for his part, was decidedly not celebrating.
sentences.zh: 至于马里奥斯，他显然并没有在庆祝。

sentences.en: He said he found the festivities downright depressing.
sentences.zh: 他说他觉得这些庆祝活动简直令人沮丧。

sentences.en: It seems to me out of control, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 在我看来这已经失控了，我不知道，

sentences.en: this sort of gray zone that we're in now politically.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在政治上处于这种灰色地带。

sentences.en: Because before we said, f*** you to the state, we're doing things our way.
sentences.zh: 因为以前我们说，去你的政府，我们按自己的方式行事。

sentences.en: But now we're in their pocket.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们被他们掌控了。

sentences.en: In their pocket, because even as most of the recent attention has been focused on Pusher Street,
sentences.zh: 被他们掌控，因为尽管最近大部分注意力都集中在普舍尔街上，

sentences.en: Christiania has struck another deal with the government that could integrate the commune with the city even more.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚又与政府达成了一项协议，这可能会使该公社与城市进一步融合。

sentences.en: Not by kicking people out, but by bringing people from the outside in.
sentences.zh: 不是通过驱逐居民，而是通过引入外部人员。

sentences.en: Denmark is struggling with an affordable housing crisis.
sentences.zh: 丹麦正面临经济适用房危机。

sentences.en: And from the government's perspective, Christiania's undeveloped land, so close to the center of the city, is ripe for development.
sentences.zh: 从政府的角度来看，克里斯蒂安尼亚未开发的土地离市中心如此之近，正是开发的绝佳地段。

sentences.en: But from Christiania's perspective, this new logic has rekindled the residents' fears of being evicted from their homes,
sentences.zh: 但从克里斯蒂安尼亚的角度来看，这种新逻辑重新点燃了居民们被赶出家园的恐惧，

sentences.en: which, remember, they do not own.
sentences.zh: 请记住，这些房子他们并不拥有所有权。

sentences.en: So, a few years ago, Christiania and the Danish government struck a bargain.
sentences.zh: 几年前，克里斯蒂安尼亚和丹麦政府达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: The state will allow for the community to own its land outright by purchasing it far below market value.
sentences.zh: 政府将允许该社区以远低于市场价值的价格购买土地，从而拥有土地的完全所有权。

sentences.en: But, in return, over the next few years,
sentences.zh: 但作为回报，在接下来的几年里，

sentences.en: Christiania will have to build government-subsidized, low-income apartments for 300 new people.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚必须为300名新居民建造政府补贴的低收入公寓。

sentences.en: Which, you might think, should solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 你可能认为这应该能解决问题。

sentences.en: Christiania has always branded itself as a place for the adrift and downtrodden.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚一直将自己标榜为漂泊者和受压迫者的避风港。

sentences.en: So, how could it possibly say no to low-income housing?
sentences.zh: 那么，它怎么可能拒绝低收入住房呢？

sentences.en: But, in reality, the deal remains highly controversial among the residents.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这项协议在居民中仍然极具争议。

sentences.en: Proving that even anarchists can go nimby.
sentences.zh: 这证明了即使是无政府主义者也会有“邻避效应”。

sentences.en: I know there's been a lot of opposition to the plan to build public housing,
sentences.zh: 我知道对于建造公共住房的计划有很多反对意见，

sentences.en: but I'm wondering if you've heard anyone express that the community should be welcoming to people living in public housing,
sentences.zh: 但我很想知道，你是否听到有人表示社区应该欢迎居住在公共住房里的人，

sentences.en: because they seem to be exactly the type of people the community has always accepted in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他们看起来正是社区过去一直接纳的那类人。

sentences.en: I don't have a problem with the people.
sentences.zh: 我对这些人本身没有意见。

sentences.en: I have a problem with the amount of people,
sentences.zh: 我对人数有意见，

sentences.en: and I have a problem especially with the volume of new buildings.
sentences.zh: 而且我特别对新建筑的数量有意见。

sentences.en: That's where I have my problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的问题所在。

sentences.en: Ollie Luke Anderson likens the plan to a Trojan horse that will ultimately destroy Christiania.
sentences.zh: 奥利·卢克·安德森（Ollie Luke Anderson）将该计划比作特洛伊木马，最终将摧毁克里斯蒂安尼亚。

sentences.en: The government's plan will increase the population by a third,
sentences.zh: 政府的计划将使人口增加三分之一，

sentences.en: and radically alter the geography of the area.
sentences.zh: 并从根本上改变该地区的地理面貌。

sentences.en: The way he puts it, the housing plan would be the equivalent of plopping down a thousand shipping containers in the middle of the community.
sentences.zh: 用他的话说，这个住房计划相当于在社区中间扔下了一千个集装箱。

sentences.en: Plus, he can't imagine how the commune will be able to work within the government's public housing bureaucracy.
sentences.zh: 此外，他无法想象公社将如何能够在政府的公共住房官僚体系下运作。

sentences.en: It will be very hard to combine the way we do stuff in Christiania with the way people do it in social housing projects.
sentences.zh: 将我们在克里斯蒂安尼亚的行事方式与人们在社会住房项目中的方式结合起来将非常困难。

sentences.en: It will not really be part of the rest of Christiania.
sentences.zh: 它将不再真正属于克里斯蒂安尼亚的一部分。

sentences.en: We'll get like two Christianias.
sentences.zh: 我们将得到两个克里斯蒂安尼亚。

sentences.en: On this issue, Marios agrees with Ollie.
sentences.zh: 在这个问题上，马里奥斯同意奥利的看法。

sentences.en: He sees both the closing of Pusher Street and the building of the affordable housing
sentences.zh: 他认为关闭普舍尔街和建造经济适用房都是同一趋势的一部分，

sentences.en: as part of the same worrying trend toward normalcy and even gentrification,
sentences.zh: 这种趋势令人担忧，即走向正常化甚至中产阶级化，

sentences.en: that Christiania's new residents will water down precisely what drew him to the community in the first place.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚的新居民会冲淡当初吸引他来到这里的特质。

sentences.en: 300 more boring people in here, or 300 more families in here not really interested in Christiania.
sentences.zh: 这里会多出300个无聊的人，或者300个对克里斯蒂安尼亚并不真正感兴趣的家庭。

sentences.en: They just want the location.
sentences.zh: 他们只是想要这个地段。

sentences.en: And as soon as all these people move in, they're going to start complaining about the noise.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些人搬进来，他们就会开始抱怨噪音。

sentences.en: Oh, the music is too loud, and then your lawn is a bit too dirty,
sentences.zh: 哦，音乐太吵了，然后你的草坪太脏了，

sentences.en: and just more and more control is going to come, and we're going to end up like everywhere else.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的控制会越来越多，最终我们会变得和其他地方一样。

sentences.en: For Marios, the community's counterculture, just like its consensus process and its tolerance towards cannabis,
sentences.zh: 对马里奥斯来说，社区的反主流文化，就像它的共识机制和对大麻的宽容一样，

sentences.en: is one of the pillars of Christiania, and he thinks it is the next to crumble.
sentences.zh: 是克里斯蒂安尼亚的支柱之一，他认为这是下一个即将崩塌的支柱。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm going to continue.
sentences.zh: 我会继续下去。

sentences.en: I'm going to continue painting and selling my art, but it'll feel maybe ironic to be
sentences.zh: 我会继续画画并出售我的艺术品，但身处一个完全商业化的环境中，

sentences.en: a rebel in the middle of something that is totally commercial.
sentences.zh: 做一个反叛者可能会显得很讽刺。

sentences.en: If they start having, you know, sort of fancy wine bars and souvenir shops,
sentences.zh: 如果他们开始出现那种高档葡萄酒吧和纪念品商店，

sentences.en: then I will start thinking where to go, you know, to find freedom again.
sentences.zh: 那么我就会开始考虑去哪里，你知道的，去寻找自由。

sentences.en: But some residents are cautiously optimistic that there might actually be a way to make this work
sentences.zh: 但一些居民谨慎地乐观认为，或许真的有一种方法可以实现这一点，

sentences.en: without sacrificing everything that's special about Christiania.
sentences.zh: 而无需牺牲克里斯蒂安尼亚所有特别的东西。

sentences.en: So in this area, we have pointed out that we could place two buildings.
sentences.zh: 在这个区域，我们已经指出可以放置两栋建筑。

sentences.en: Meta Prague has lived in Christiania for nearly 40 years,
sentences.zh: 梅塔·布拉格（Meta Prague）在克里斯蒂安尼亚居住了近40年，

sentences.en: and toward the end of my visit, she gave me a tour of some of the proposed sites for the new housing.
sentences.zh: 在我访问快结束时，她带我参观了一些拟建住房的地点。

sentences.en: At the moment, it's an open space where we have storage for woods and some very beautiful trees.
sentences.zh: 目前，这是一个开放空间，我们用来存放木材，还有一些非常漂亮的树。

sentences.en: On the other side, they have a nice garden for this huge building over there.
sentences.zh: 在另一边，他们为那边那栋巨大的建筑提供了一个不错的花园。

sentences.en: They have a public garden.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个公共花园。

sentences.en: So a lot of this would be demolished to make way for the housing.
sentences.zh: 所以大部分地方将被拆除，为住房腾出空间。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Meta has a background in architecture and urban renewal,
sentences.zh: 梅塔有建筑和城市更新的背景，

sentences.en: and lately, she's been using her experience to help the community negotiate the terms of its housing agreement with the Danish government.
sentences.zh: 最近，她一直利用自己的经验帮助社区与丹麦政府协商住房协议的条款。

sentences.en: One of the challenges, Meta explains, is that for a long time now,
sentences.zh: 梅塔解释说，挑战之一在于，长期以来，

sentences.en: Christiania has had a specific process to carefully vet new people before they move into the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚在新人搬入社区之前，一直有一套特定的程序来仔细审查他们。

sentences.en: Nowadays, when we have an empty house and invite people to apply for it,
sentences.zh: 如今，当我们有空房子并邀请人们申请时，

sentences.en: we are free to choose who will come and live here,
sentences.zh: 我们可以自由选择谁来这里居住，

sentences.en: to choose outcasts, spacey-thinking people who will fit to the house beSt.
sentences.zh: 选择那些最适合这里的局外人、思想天马行空的人。

sentences.en: For example, what could this person give back to the community?
sentences.zh: 例如，这个人能为社区做出什么贡献？

sentences.en: Are they a good carpenter?
sentences.zh: 他们是优秀的木匠吗？

sentences.en: Are they a skilled gardener who will take care of the neighborhood's green spaces?
sentences.zh: 他们是能照顾社区绿地的熟练园丁吗？

sentences.en: Maybe they're good at planning meetings and events.
sentences.zh: 也许他们擅长策划会议和活动。

sentences.en: With people applying for public housing, those factors would no longer matter.
sentences.zh: 随着人们申请公共住房，这些因素将不再重要。

sentences.en: Still, Meta says there are creative loopholes the community can use to navigate this new bureaucratic system,
sentences.zh: 不过，梅塔说，社区可以利用创造性的漏洞来应对这种新的官僚体系，

sentences.en: and she's ready to deal with the challenge head-on.
sentences.zh: 她已经准备好直面这一挑战。

sentences.en: I think you just have to face it that it will, Christiania will change with new inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须面对现实，克里斯蒂安尼亚会随着新居民的到来而改变。

sentences.en: And the question is, do Christiania need new inhabitants?
sentences.zh: 问题是，克里斯蒂安尼亚需要新居民吗？

sentences.en: Or can we go on like we are today?
sentences.zh: 还是我们可以像今天这样继续下去？

sentences.en: And basically, I think that in all communities, you need to always be developing.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我认为在所有社区中，你都需要不断发展。

sentences.en: So you always have to be in a kind of dialogue with the outside, inside, outside, inside.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须始终与外部保持某种对话，内部、外部，内部、外部。

sentences.en: Because otherwise, you will slowly die.
sentences.zh: 因为否则，你就会慢慢死去。

sentences.en: Despite some of the opposition to the new housing, this was another sentiment I heard a lot.
sentences.zh: 尽管对新住房有一些反对意见，但这也是我经常听到的另一种观点。

sentences.en: That change itself isn't inherently something to be afraid of.
sentences.zh: 改变本身并不一定是值得害怕的事情。

sentences.en: Christiania cannot end up as a hippie museum, kind of, right?
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚不能最终变成一个嬉皮士博物馆，对吧？

sentences.en: John Van Carlsen no longer lives in Christiania, but he agrees with Meta Prague.
sentences.zh: 约翰·范·卡尔森（John Van Carlsen）虽然不再住在克里斯蒂安尼亚，但他同意梅塔·布拉格的观点。

sentences.en: He believes that the only real mistake is not changing.
sentences.zh: 他认为唯一真正的错误就是不改变。

sentences.en: If they build buildings where ordinary people can come in, old people, young people, lonely mothers,
sentences.zh: 如果他们建造普通人可以进来的建筑，老年人、年轻人、单身母亲，

sentences.en: I think that Christiania should trust in the strengths of its own spirit to a degree that they're not afraid of being wiped out by incoming people.
sentences.zh: 我认为克里斯蒂安尼亚应该相信自己精神的力量，达到某种程度，让他们不至于害怕被新来的人抹去。

sentences.en: It should develop with the surrounding society.
sentences.zh: 它应该与周围的社会共同发展。

sentences.en: The truth is, for all of Christiania's efforts to exist separate and apart from the world,
sentences.zh: 事实是，尽管克里斯蒂安尼亚努力与世界保持独立和隔绝，

sentences.en: this place has never really been able to be as completely independent as its founders had envisioned all those years ago.
sentences.zh: 这个地方从来没有真正像创始人在多年前设想的那样完全独立。

sentences.en: I ran this by John and Ole, and they were quick to agree.
sentences.zh: 我把这个想法告诉了约翰和奥勒，他们很快表示赞同。

sentences.en: Of course, it has been a grand illusion to think that Christiania, at any point, was separated from the world.
sentences.zh: 当然，认为克里斯蒂安尼亚在任何时候都与世界隔绝，这一直是一个宏大的幻觉。

sentences.en: Christiania is very much a normal part of Denmark.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚在很大程度上是丹麦正常的一部分。

sentences.en: It's still a bit different as a neighborhood, but it's part of the reSt.
sentences.zh: 作为一个社区，它仍然有点不同，但它是整体的一部分。

sentences.en: Christiania will even have to take out a bank loan to buy the land and build the new housing.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安尼亚甚至不得不向银行贷款来购买土地并建造新住房。

sentences.en: They'll make their money back by charging the new tenants rent.
sentences.zh: 他们将通过向新租户收取租金来收回成本。

sentences.en: Things like interest rates, inflation, and the real estate market?
sentences.zh: 比如利率、通货膨胀和房地产市场这些问题？

sentences.en: These things now matter just as much within the walls of Christiania as anywhere else in the EU.
sentences.zh: 如今，这些问题在克里斯蒂安尼亚内部和欧盟其他任何地方一样重要。

sentences.en: In the end, it's clear that the world's problems have also become Christiania's probleMs.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，显而易见的是，世界面临的问题也成了克里斯蒂安尼亚的问题。

sentences.en: But John says that even if the community can't totally escape from all the different pressures,
sentences.zh: 但约翰说，即使社区无法完全摆脱各种压力，

sentences.en: that doesn't make it any less of an achievement.
sentences.zh: 这也不影响它取得的成就。

sentences.en: So if Christiania were to close tomorrow, would you look back at it and think it's been a success?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果克里斯蒂安尼亚明天就要关闭，你会回首往事，认为它成功了吗？

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I certainly would.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会。

sentences.en: I certainly would.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会。

sentences.en: I think Christiania's impact, apart from being a beautiful urban flower that you are entertained by
sentences.zh: 我认为克里斯蒂安尼亚的影响力，除了它是一朵让你感到愉悦、

sentences.en: and like the smell of, it's that all of us have the power, if we are courageous enough,
sentences.zh: 闻起来芬芳的城市之花外，还在于我们每个人都有能力，只要足够勇敢，

sentences.en: to create our own surroundings.
sentences.zh: 就能创造属于自己的环境。

sentences.en: That we can decide our own way of living.
sentences.zh: 我们能够决定自己的生活方式。

sentences.en: You know, we can actually kick down the walls to get out in the open air.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们实际上可以推倒围墙，走向广阔的天地。

sentences.en: And at least try to do it, right?
sentences.zh: 至少尝试去这样做，对吧？

sentences.zh: 凯利·普莱姆、雅各布·马尔多纳多-梅迪纳、尼娜·波托克，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: The 99% Invisible logo was created by Stefan Lawrence.
sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》的标志由斯特凡·劳伦斯创作。

sentences.en: We are part of the Stitcher and SiriusXM podcast family,
sentences.zh: 我们是 Stitcher 和 SiriusXM 播客家族的一员，

sentences.en: now headquartered six blocks north in the Pandora Building,
sentences.zh: 现在总部位于北边六个街区外的潘多拉大厦，

sentences.en: in beautiful Uptown, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 坐落在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽的住宅区。

sentences.en: Home of the Oakland Roots Soccer Club, of which I'm a proud community owner.
sentences.zh: 这里也是奥克兰根基足球俱乐部的主场，我很自豪能成为该社区的所有者之一。

sentences.en: Other teams may come and go, but the roots are Oakland first, always.
sentences.zh: 其他球队可能会来来去去，但根基永远属于奥克兰。

sentences.en: You can find us on all the usual social media sites,
sentences.zh: 你可以在所有常见的社交媒体网站上找到我们，

sentences.en: as well as our new Discord server, where we talk about the Power Broker,
sentences.zh: 还有我们新的 Discord 服务器，我们在那里讨论《权力掮客》，

sentences.en: we talk about episodes, we talk about architecture, we talk about flags,
sentences.zh: 讨论剧集，讨论建筑，讨论旗帜，

sentences.en: we talk about all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: There's a link to that Discord server,
sentences.zh: 那个 Discord 服务器有一个链接，

sentences.en: as well as every past episode of 99PI at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 以及《99PI》过去的所有剧集都可以在 99PI.org 上找到。
